text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today, continuing a sharp four-day rally that's recovered most of last week's losses. The bounce reflects a modest lift in oil prices—US crude moved to $89.62 per barrel—but more importantly, it caps a rebound from a two-week dip that had taken the stock down 7.6%. The stock gained $5.69 in the last four trading days alone, suggesting investors are regaining confidence in energy after a recent pullback.

The broader backdrop is mixed for oil demand. Heating oil prices have spiked 59% from last winter, which normally signals strong demand, but Russia's crude production has rebounded sharply to 8.73 million barrels a day following a diesel deal, pushing global oil markets back into surplus—meaning more supply than the world needs right now. That tension between tight heating demand and rising Russian supply may explain why the stock recovered steadily rather than surging: there's no clear tailwind, just a rebound from oversold levels.
